species.name: Gray wolf
species.fact: Every domestic dog alive descends from an ancient population of these.

species.name: Red fox
species.fact: Dives nose-first into snow after mice, and appears to line the jump up using Earth's magnetic field.

species.name: Fennec fox
species.fact: Ears up to 15 cm long, the largest of any canid relative to body size, and they work as radiators.

species.name: Arctic fox
species.fact: The warmest coat of any mammal. It does not start shivering until about -70 C.

credit.artist_html: Jonatan Pie (unsplash.com/@r3dmax)

species.name: African wild dog
species.fact: Packs decide when to set off hunting by sneezing. Enough sneezes and the vote carries.

species.name: Bat-eared fox
species.fact: Listens for termites underground and has up to 50 teeth, more than any other placental land mammal.

species.name: Dhole
species.fact: An Asian wild dog that whistles to keep the pack together.

species.name: Maned wolf
species.fact: Not a wolf and not a fox, but a long-legged canid all of its own. Its urine smells strongly of cannabis.

credit.artist_html: Jonathan Wilkins

species.name: Raccoon dog
species.fact: A true canid wearing a raccoon's face. The only one that climbs trees and sleeps through the winter.

species.name: Brown bear
species.fact: Bears sit on the dog-like branch of Carnivora, closest to seals and weasels.

species.name: Polar bear
species.fact: The fur is transparent rather than white, and the skin underneath is black.

credit.artist_html: Christopher Michel
credit.file_name: Polar Bear with its tongue sticking out.jpg

species.name: Giant panda
species.fact: A bear running a 99% bamboo diet on a carnivore's gut, which is why it must eat up to 38 kg of it a day.

species.name: Sun bear
species.fact: The smallest bear, with a 25 cm tongue for emptying honeycombs and termite nests.

species.name: Sloth bear
species.fact: Missing its two upper front teeth, leaving a gap it uses to vacuum termites out of their mounds.

species.name: Wolverine
species.fact: A 15 kg weasel with the confidence to drive bears off a carcass.

species.name: Sea otter
species.fact: The densest fur of any animal, up to a million hairs per square inch, and it holds hands while sleeping.

credit.artist_html: Marshal Hedin from San Diego

species.name: Honey badger
species.fact: Loose rubbery skin lets it rotate inside its own hide and bite whatever has it by the neck.

credit.artist_html: Sumeet Moghe

species.name: European badger
species.fact: Digs setts that stay in use by generation after generation for over a century.

credit.artist_html: Charles J. Sharp

species.name: Stoat
species.fact: Turns white in winter, at which point the coat gets sold as ermine.

credit.artist_html: Marton Berntsen, crop by User:MPF

species.name: Eurasian otter
species.fact: Otters are aquatic weasels, and weasels are firmly on the dog-like branch.

species.name: Pine marten
species.fact: Cat-shaped, cat-sized, cat-agile, and a mustelid.

species.name: Raccoon
species.fact: Its front paws carry four times the touch receptors of the hind ones. It largely sees by feel.

species.name: Kinkajou
species.fact: A carnivoran that mostly eats fruit, hangs by a prehensile tail, and pollinates flowers with a 13 cm tongue.

species.name: South American coati
species.fact: Females and young roam in bands of up to 30 while adult males live alone.

species.name: Ringtail
species.fact: Nicknamed the miner's cat and the ring-tailed cat. It is a raccoon relative and no kind of cat.

species.name: Striped skunk
species.fact: Sprays accurately to about 3 metres, but stamps its front feet in warning first.

species.name: Red panda
species.fact: Not a bear, not a raccoon, and not related to the giant panda. The only living member of its family, and it sits on the dog-like branch.

species.name: Harbour seal
species.fact: Its whiskers can follow the wake a fish left behind up to 30 seconds earlier.

credit.artist_html: Charles J. Sharp

species.name: Leopard seal
species.fact: Named for a cat, related to weasels and bears. It sings underwater for hours at a time.

species.name: Northern elephant seal
species.fact: Dives to 1,500 m and can stay under for nearly two hours.

species.name: California sea lion
species.fact: Unlike true seals it can swing its hind flippers forward and gallop on land.

credit.artist: (c) Jonathan Eisen, some rights reserved (CC BY)
credit.artist_html: (c) Jonathan Eisen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

species.name: Walrus
species.fact: Those tusks are canine teeth up to a metre long, used to haul two tonnes of walrus onto the ice.

species.name: Lion
species.fact: The only cat that lives in groups. The roar carries about 8 km.

species.name: Tiger
species.fact: The stripes are on the skin as well as the fur. Shave one and the pattern is still there.

credit.artist_html: Charles J. Sharp

species.name: Cheetah
species.fact: Semi-retractable claws act as sprint spikes. Nought to 100 km/h in about three seconds.

species.name: Snow leopard
species.fact: Cannot roar, and uses its metre-long tail as a blanket.

species.name: Jaguar
species.fact: The strongest bite of any big cat for its size. It kills by punching through the skull.

species.name: Serval
species.fact: The longest legs of any cat relative to its body, and it leaps 3 m to pluck birds out of the air.

species.name: Caracal
species.fact: Twenty muscles in each tufted ear, and it knocks birds down mid-leap.

species.name: Sand cat
species.fact: Fur-covered foot pads let it cross 60 C sand, and it never needs to drink.

species.name: Clouded leopard
species.fact: Canines as long as a tiger's relative to its skull, and it can climb down a trunk head-first.

species.name: Black-footed cat
species.fact: Africa's smallest cat and its deadliest. Roughly 60% of its hunts succeed.

credit.artist: Patrick Ch. Apfeld , derivative editing by Poke2001
credit.artist_html: Patrick Ch. Apfeld, derivative editing by Poke2001

species.name: Ocelot
species.fact: A cat that swims willingly, which most of the family will not.

species.name: Eurasian lynx
species.fact: Europe's third largest predator, and the ear tufts work as hearing aids.

species.name: Cougar
species.fact: Cannot roar but purrs like a house cat, and holds the record for the most names of any animal.

species.name: Fishing cat
species.fact: Taps the water surface to imitate insects, then dives in after the fish that come to look.

species.name: Spotted hyena
species.fact: Far closer to cats than to dogs. Clans are run by females, and every female outranks every male.

credit.artist_html: Charles J. Sharp

species.name: Striped hyena
species.fact: Hyenas branched off the cat-like side of Carnivora. The dog resemblance is pure convergent evolution.

species.name: Aardwolf
species.fact: A hyena, therefore a cat-like carnivoran, despite the name. It eats up to 300,000 termites a night.

species.name: Meerkat
species.fact: A mongoose, not a cat, whatever the name says. Sentries use different alarm calls for hawks and for snakes.

credit.artist_html: Charles J. Sharp

species.name: Banded mongoose
species.fact: Mongooses are cat-like carnivorans, and the whole pack gives birth on the same night.

species.name: Indian grey mongoose
species.fact: Its acetylcholine receptors are shaped so that cobra venom cannot lock on.

species.name: Binturong
species.fact: Known as the bearcat, it is neither, and its scent glands smell convincingly of hot buttered popcorn.

species.name: Common genet
species.fact: Looks like a spotted cat but belongs to the civets, and can flatten itself through any gap its head fits.

credit.artist_html: Guérin Nicolas (messages)

species.name: Asian palm civet
species.fact: The animal behind kopi luwak coffee.

credit.artist_html: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE

species.name: African civet
species.fact: Its musk was a base note in perfume for centuries.

credit.file_name: African civet, South Luangwa National Park (51866143791).jpg

species.name: Fossa
species.fact: Madagascar's top predator. Looks like a puma crossed with a mongoose, and mongooses are the closer guess.

credit.artist_html: Ran Kirlian

species.name: African palm civet
species.fact: The only member of its family. Its lineage split off before every other cat-like carnivoran.

species.name: Banded linsang
species.fact: The closest living relative of the true cats, sitting in a family of its own.
